source.title_on_document: Generative AI and Student Creativity: Cognitive Scaffolding Tool or Constraint on Originality? An Empirical Investigation in Vietnamese Higher Education

supplement.where: The document does not refer to any supplement, online appendix, data, or code.
supplement.holds: Nothing referenced. All statistics on file are in the main text (Tables 1-3 and Sections 4.1-4.3).

paper_design_summary: 480 undergraduates at three Vietnamese universities were assigned in a randomized between-subjects design to three conditions of 160 each: unaided control (no devices or AI), unconstrained access to an LLM (GPT-4o / Claude 3.5 Sonnet), or the same LLM used under a structured scaffolding protocol (own ideas first, then critique prompts, no copying). In one 90-minute session they did an alternative-solutions task (microplastic pollution in the Mekong Delta) and wrote a 600-word campaign brief. Two trained raters scored fluency, flexibility, and elaboration; six experts rated originality, appropriateness, and overall creativity (CAT, 1-7); pairwise cosine similarity of text-embedding-3-large embeddings measured homogenization within each condition.

studies.label: Three-arm experiment (unaided control vs unconstrained GenAI vs structured scaffolding), Vietnamese undergraduates

assignment.what_was_assigned: Condition: unaided control, unconstrained GenAI access, or structured scaffolding (CARP protocol) with the same LLM
assignment.quote: The quantitative phase deployed a randomized between-subjects experimental design with three conditions
assignment.locator: PDF p. 4 (printed p. 182), Section 3.1 Experimental Design; also Abstract, PDF p. 1: 'under three randomized experimental conditions'

arms.name: Unaided Control
arms.description: Creative tasks with no digital devices, search engines, or AI interfaces.

arms.name: Unconstrained GenAI Access
arms.description: Unmonitored access to an LLM interface (GPT-4o / Claude 3.5 Sonnet), told 'You may use the AI tool in any manner you choose to complete this task.'

arms.name: Structured Scaffolding
arms.description: Same LLM, used under the Cognitive Anchor-Rebound Protocol: Phase A at least three own ideas before opening the interface; Phase B critique and counter-factual prompts; Phase C synthesis without copying AI text.

participants.exclusions: None reported. Design section gives n = 160 per condition; Table 1 reports N = 480 with n = 160 per arm.
participants.who: Undergraduates from Vietnam National University (Hanoi), The University of Danang, and Ho Chi Minh City University of Technology (HUTECH); 160 each in humanities and social sciences, business and management, and design, media and technology; 58.3% female; mean age 20.4 (SD 1.35).
participants.quote: A total of 480 undergraduate students participated across three broad disciplinary clusters.
participants.locator: PDF p. 4-5 (printed pp. 182-183), Section 3.2 Participants and Sampling Matrix; Table 1 title 'N = 480', PDF p. 6

ai_tool.name_model: GPT-4o / Claude 3.5 Sonnet (LLM interface; which model each participant used is not stated)
ai_tool.how_used: Unconstrained arm: free use of the chatbot in any manner. Scaffolded arm: same interface under a mandated protocol (own ideas first, then critique and counter-factual prompts, then synthesis without copying AI text), closer to refinement/critique of the student's own ideas.

task.description: Task 1: Alternative Solutions Task, proposing sustainable solutions to urban microplastic contamination in the Mekong Delta agricultural belt. Task 2: a 600-word conceptual campaign brief for a socio-technological enterprise addressing rural education equity in Vietnam.
task.duration: Both tasks within one 90-minute timed session

outcomes.name: Intra-group mean pairwise cosine similarity (semantic dispersion index = 1 - CosSim)
outcomes.question: across_people
outcomes.measure_detail: Submissions embedded with OpenAI text-embedding-3-large (1536 dimensions); pairwise cosine similarity among all submissions within the same task and condition. Higher similarity = homogenization. Which task Table 2 refers to is not stated. Sign reversed for diversity: higher similarity means less diverse.

contrasts.reported: Mean pairwise cosine similarity (SD): Unaided Control 0.412 (0.084), dispersion 0.588; Unconstrained GenAI 0.689 (0.061), dispersion 0.311; t(318) = 34.21, p < .001, d = 3.79. Direction coded for diversity (similarity higher in treatment). n per arm 160 (Table 1); n of similarity scores not stated.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 7 (printed p. 185), Table 2 and Section 4.2

contrasts.reported: Structured Scaffolding 0.465 (0.072), dispersion 0.535 vs Control 0.412 (0.084), dispersion 0.588; no test reported. Direction coded for diversity (similarity slightly higher in treatment). Text calls the scaffolded group's dispersion 'high'.

diversity_detail.metric: Mean pairwise cosine similarity within condition (SD); Semantic Dispersion Index = 1 - CosSim
diversity_detail.computed_over: All pairs of student submissions within the same task and condition ('pairwise cosine similarity among all student submissions within the same task')
diversity_detail.uncertainty: Independent-samples t-test, t(318) = 34.21 for Unconstrained vs Control; df of 318 suggests one score per submission (160 per arm), but the paper does not say how a per-submission score was built. No test for the other contrasts.
diversity_detail.notes: The MANOVA lists 'Semantic Distance' as a primary dependent variable (Section 4.1), but Table 1 has no semantic-distance row; only Table 2 reports it.

company_involvement.description: Single academic author (University of Education, Vietnam National University). Uses commercial LLMs and OpenAI embeddings; no company funding or authorship stated.

eligibility.reason: As written, the paper reports a randomized between-subjects design (p. 182, Section 3.1) assigning 480 undergraduates (160 per arm, Table 1) to no AI, unconstrained LLM, or scaffolded LLM, with expert CAT ratings, rater-coded TTCT counts, and embedding similarity scored on their outputs. On the stated design all three criteria are met. The randomization procedure itself is not described, and the paper has serious internal inconsistencies (see open_questions) that the audit should weigh before any estimate is used.

one_line_finding: Unconstrained LLM access raised fluency (11.45 vs 5.12 ideas) but lowered expert-rated originality (3.41 vs 4.82 on a 1-7 CAT scale, d = -1.34) and raised within-group cosine similarity (0.689 vs 0.412), while structured scaffolding gave the highest originality (5.44) and overall creativity (5.51) (Table 1, p. 184; Table 2, p. 185).
open_questions: Abstract and body disagree: fluency F(2,477) = 48.21, eta^2 = .168 in the Abstract vs F(2,477) = 284.15, eta^2 = .543 in Table 1; originality d = -0.58 in the Abstract vs d = -1.34 in Section 4.1 for the same Unconstrained vs Control contrast.

Table 3 (p. 185) shows Unconstrained Prompt Count -.241 with no star and Iterative Counter-Prompts .389*, while the text (p. 186) gives p < .01 and p < .001 for these; text says the predictors 'accounted for 45.8%' while the table shows R^2 = .468 and adjusted R^2 = .458.

The randomization procedure is not described beyond 'randomized between-subjects'; Section 3.2 describes 'stratified random sampling' for recruitment. Exactly 160 per arm and 160 per discipline cluster.

The reference list is truncated mid-entry ('Bose#', p. 190) and lacks many works cited in the text (e.g., Torrance 1966, Vygotsky 1978, Jansson & Smith 1991). Together with the very large effects (d = 3.79 for similarity) this raises a question about the paper's reliability that the audit should consider.

Which task (Alternative Solutions Task or 600-word brief) each Table 1 and Table 2 measure comes from is only partly stated: CAT ratings are on the project briefs; the TTCT coding covers 'all submissions'; the embedding analysis is 'within the same task' without naming it.
MANOVA names Semantic Distance as a primary DV, but it is not in Table 1; the semantic t-test df (318) implies per-submission scores whose construction is not described.
notes: PDF pages 1-12 correspond to printed pages 179-190; locators give both. Not coded as outcomes: Table 3 hierarchical regression predicting originality among the 320 AI users (process predictors, not an arm contrast; Model 3: verbatim AI text retention beta = -.442***, pre-AI ideation time .318***); qualitative findings that 88.4% of unconstrained students built on one of the AI's five options and that recurring themes appeared in 71% of unconstrained essays (p. 186, no comparison arm statistic). Qualitative interviews with 36 participants (12 per condition). Preregistration not mentioned. Limitations (p. 189) describe outputs as 'immediate creative output within laboratory conditions'.
